writer_capabilities.atomic_checkpoint_save: tmp + os.replace in same dir (tools/vector_indexer.py:225 save_checkpoint)
writer_capabilities.stage_commit_atomicity: NOT atomic — manifest.json + vectors.jsonl + commit.json written sequentially with Path.write_text; mid-stage crash can leave partial dir, but content-addressed commit_id makes retry idempotent (overwrites same dir)
writer_capabilities.fsync_or_dir_sync: none — relying on OS-level os.replace atomicity for the rename only; data buffers are not explicitly flushed to durable storage
writer_capabilities.concurrent_writer_assumption: implicit single-writer; emit() opens in append mode without advisory lock
writer_capabilities.checksum: sha256 over sorted (rel_path, content_sha256) pairs in commit dir, computed via _checksum_dir; commit.json itself is excluded from the input

event_log_capabilities.format: JSONL (one canonical event per line, sorted keys, compact separators)
event_log_capabilities.writer: vector_events.emit() opens 'a', writes line + newline, closes; vector_events.emit_many() batches in single open
event_log_capabilities.reader: vector_events.read_events() iterates lines, json.loads each, constructs VectorEvent; missing file → empty iterator
event_log_capabilities.malformed_line_policy: SILENT SKIP — read_events catches json.JSONDecodeError on parse and KeyError/ValueError on construction, continues
event_log_capabilities.deduplication: VectorEvent.event_id() excludes ts so same content yields same id — but writer does NOT dedup; consumer must dedup if needed
event_log_capabilities.schema_version: VECTOR_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1; old v1 events without 'source' field still parse (defaults to None)

known_failure_surfaces.F1_mid_stage_write: manifest, vectors, or commit.json partial write — retry is idempotent because commit_id is content-addressed and stage path is deterministic
known_failure_surfaces.F2_mid_checksum: _checksum_dir crashes mid-rglob — commit.json not written, prior current.json untouched, retry recomputes
known_failure_surfaces.F3_before_swap: post-stage, pre-os.replace — staged dir exists with manifest + vectors + commit.json but pointer still points to prior commit; retry stages same content, swaps cleanly
known_failure_surfaces.F4_after_swap_before_emit: pointer advanced to new commit but no vector.commit_applied event emitted; rerun re-stages (idempotent) + re-swaps (idempotent — same content) + emits event for the first time. NOTE: this means a successful first run plus a between-swap-and-emit crash can produce two emits if the crash happens between emit and checkpoint save (see F5)
known_failure_surfaces.F5_after_emit_before_checkpoint: event row in log but checkpoint not advanced; rerun reads checkpoint (still points at prior id) → folds events including the just-emitted commit_applied → recomputes the same commit_id → re-emits a duplicate vector.commit_applied event. event_id is identical (excludes ts) — duplicate detection is the consumer's responsibility, but the duplicate is harmless because commit content is byte-identical
known_failure_surfaces.F6_malformed_row: json.JSONDecodeError or KeyError/ValueError on construction → silently skipped by read_events; later events still applied; projection becomes a function of valid rows only
known_failure_surfaces.F7_pointer_swap_partial_on_windows: os.replace is documented atomic on both POSIX and Windows; no known partial-replace failure mode in normal operation
known_failure_surfaces.F8_multi_writer_append_interleave: POSIX append-mode write atomicity holds up to PIPE_BUF (~4096 bytes) for raw write; Python text-mode buffering can break this. On Windows, FILE_APPEND_DATA is single-write atomic. Best-effort either way; not portable to assume cross-platform atomic concurrent emit().
known_failure_surfaces.F9_truncation_or_shrink_of_temp_artifact: if a tmp file in the same dir is truncated by another writer between Path.write_text and os.replace, the swap promotes a corrupt file. No protection in current code.

current_event_semantics: at_least_once_but_idempotent_per_commit (proven via inspection of apply() ordering — see chosen_event_semantics rationale)
current_checkpoint_semantics: global checkpoint advances after at least one cell applied; per-cell checkpoint advances inline within the try-block before global save; checkpoint is durable via tmp + os.replace
chosen_event_semantics_rationale: exact_once_per_commit cannot be proven without either a two-phase commit journal or a transactional write+emit. Current design relies on (a) content-addressed commit_id from compute_commit_id (deterministic, hash of cell_state.signatures), (b) atomic pointer swap via os.replace, and (c) atomic checkpoint via os.replace. Failure between swap and emit, or between emit and checkpoint, leads to a redundant event on rerun — but the duplicate has the same event_id (event_id excludes ts) and the same commit content. So the contract is at-least-once with idempotent payload semantics. Consumers must dedup by event_id or commit_id if exact-once observable behavior is required.

key_observations_from_tests.duplicate_commit_applied_event_ids_diffe: When emit succeeds but checkpoint save crashes, the second-pass apply re-emits a commit_applied event for the same logical commit. The duplicate shares faiss_commit_id, checksum, vector_count, and source_events list, BUT input_event_range can shift because the first pass's just-emitted commit_applied is itself an event in the log when the second pass folds. Idempotency is therefore at the COMMIT-CONTENT level, not the EVENT-IDENTITY level. Will be documented in VECTOR_WRITER_RESILIENCE.md.
